Types of Constructivism, Informative Diagram, elements: Three sections labeled: 'Cognitive', 'Social', and 'Radical', each with a brief description of their focus on learning. Informative icons accompany each section.

```mermaid flowchart TB %% Types of Constructivism (Informative Diagram) H["3 TYPES OF
CONSTRUCTIVISM
THAT YOU CAN USE"] subgraph C1["1 Cognitive"] direction LR I1["🧠⚙️"] T1["Cognitive constructivism focuses on the idea that learning should be related to the learner's stage of cognitive development.

These methods help learners learn new information by connecting it to things they already know, enabling them to modify their existing intelligence to accommodate the new information."] I1 --- T1 end subgraph C2["2 Social"] direction LR I2["👥🧩"] T2["Social constructivism focuses on the collaborative nature of learning. Knowledge develops from how people interact with each other, their culture, and society at large.

Learners rely on others to help create their building blocks, and learning from others helps them construct their own knowledge and reality."] I2 --- T2 end subgraph C3["3 Radical"] direction LR I3["🕸️⭕"] T3["Radical constructivism is very different from cognitive and social constructivism. Solow Growth Model - Effect of Technology, Graph, elements: Graph showing two curves representing capital per worker over time, with annotations for higher technology level effects. Key points labeled: k(0), k*, and k(2). Growth determinants and Solow growth equations noted.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  %% Solow Growth Model - Change in Technology (A)

  subgraph G["Solow Growth Model - Effect of Technology (A)"]
    direction LR

    subgraph P["Graph: Determinants of Δk/k vs k (capital per worker)"]
      direction TB
      A0["y-axis: Determinants of Δk/k"]:::axis
      X0["x-axis: k = K/L (capital per worker)"]:::axis

      dep["(δ + n)  (break-even investment)"]:::hline

      sA1["sA₁·f(k)/k  (lower technology)"]:::curveLow
      sA2["sA₂·f(k)/k  (higher technology)"]:::curveHigh

      note1["Upper curve has higher technology level than lower curve"]:::note

      k0["k(0)"]:::kp
      k1["k*₁"]:::kp
      k2["k*₂"]:::kp

      k0 --- dep
      k1 --- dep
      k2 --- dep

      k0 -.-> sA1
      k1 -.-> sA1
      k2 -.-> sA2

      sA2 --> note1
    end

    subgraph R["Analysis"]
      direction TB
      ex["Example: Advance in finance theory / computer technology in 1970s (discrete advance)"]:::note
      a1["1. In short run, advance in technology (A) boosts growth rates of capital per worker and GDP per capita."]:::bullet
      a2["2. Growth rates remain higher during transition to steady state."]:::bullet
      a3["3. In long run, growth rates of capital and real GDP per worker fall to zero."]:::bullet
      a4["4. In steady state, higher technology raises steady-state capital per worker (k*₂ > k*₁) and real GDP per capita (y*), not growth rates (remain = 0)."]:::bullet
    end

    subgraph Q["Recall"]
      direction TB
      q1["Production Function:  y = A·f(k)"]:::eq
      q2["Solow Growth Equation:  Δk/k = s·[A·f(k)]/k − δ − n"]:::eq
    end
  end

  classDef axis fill:#ffffff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
  classDef hline fill:#e6f2ff,stroke:#1f77b4,stroke-width:3px;
  classDef curveLow fill:#ffffff,stroke:#2ca02c,stroke-width:3px;
  classDef curveHigh fill:#ffffff,stroke:#d62728,stroke-width:3px,stroke-dasharray:6 4;
  classDef kp fill:#ffffff,stroke:#666,stroke-width:1px;
  classDef note fill:#fff7cc,stroke:#b59b00,stroke-width:1px;
  classDef bullet fill:#ffffff,stroke:#bbb,stroke-width:1px;
  classDef eq fill:#f7f7ff,stroke:#6666aa,stroke-width:1px;
```
